lines: We estimate that global lithium demand could grow by approximately 30% in 2026, and expect the market could surpass 3 million metric tons by 2030.
However, higher fertilizer prices have led some farmers to moderate their purchasing activity, prompting us to adjust our full-year sales volume growth outlook to approximately 5%.
Looking ahead, we expect sales volumes to increase during the fourth quarter, allowing us to close 2026 with full-year sales volumes approximately 20% above 2025 levels.

In light of these market dynamics, we are revising our full-year 2026 sales volume growth outlook for this business line to approximately 5%, compared to our previous expectation of approximately 10% growth over 2025.
We expect demand to remain robust and estimate that global iodine demand could grow over 3% in 2027 compared to 2026, mainly driven by continued demand for X-ray contrast media.

desk.headline: Revenue up 80% to $2.11bn and EPS $1.91, both below estimates; warns Q4 lithium price could be substantially lower and cuts plant-nutrition volume outlook
results: Revenue rose 80% to $2.11bn, about 4% short of the $2.19bn estimate; net income tripled to $544.2m, or $1.91 a share (estimate $1.97).
Lithium drove the jump: revenue up 151% to $1.52bn on prices more than double a year ago, but the realised price fell 10% from Q2 to about $19.6/kg.
Lithium volumes rose 8% to 78.9k tonnes; Chilean (Novandino) sales were up 16%, while Australian spodumene sales fell 54% on shipment timing.
Iodine revenue rose 7% to $262.0m and plant-nutrition revenue 4% to $269.1m, though plant-nutrition volumes fell 13% as high fertiliser prices slowed buying.
Gross profit nearly tripled to $963.8m and adjusted EBITDA rose 157% to $1.03bn; cash stood at $2.69bn at 30 September.

guidance.summary: SQM cut its 2026 plant-nutrition volume growth outlook to about 5% from about 10%, and warned its Q4 realised lithium price could be substantially lower than Q3 after a sharp market fall. It gives no revenue or profit forecast; on the call management kept its roughly $3bn 2026–2028 spending plan.

items.new: could be substantially lower than Q3

points: CEO Ricardo Ramos said lower prices give no reason to change the spending plan; the CFO put 2026–2028 capex near $3bn, with under $500m spent in nine months.
Management could not say when lithium prices will recover and said today's price looks below the level needed to attract new supply.
Novandino (the Codelco venture) expects close to 290k tonnes of lithium in 2026 and a little over 300k tonnes in 2027.
SQM sees lithium demand of close to 2.5m tonnes in 2027, growth of 15–20%; extra capacity in Chile or China is under study but not decided.
call.source: Call coverage: The Rio Times, 19 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)
